chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from al-Ḥasan, from Zurʿah, from Samāʿah, from Abī Baṣīr, who said:

I asked him about banishment from the land—how is it? He said: “He is banished from all the lands of Islam. Then if he is apprehended in any part of the land of Islam, he is killed, and there is no security for him until he joins the land of shirk.”

key_terms.أَرْضِ الشِّرْكِ: the land of shirk, outside the domain of Islam
key_terms.أَرْضِ الْإِسْلَامِ: any territory belonging to the domain of Islam
key_terms.الْأَرْضِ: the land or territory under discussion
key_terms.الْإِنْفَاءِ: banishment or exile as a legal punishment
key_terms.بِلَادِ الْإِسْلَامِ: the lands of Islam from which the person is expelled

ai.seo_question: How is banishment from the land carried out in Shia hadith law?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the legal ruling of exile as a punishment, stating that the person is to be expelled from all the lands of Islam. If he is found anywhere in the land of Islam after that, he is to be killed, and he is granted no security until he reaches the land of shirk.
